How Chimera Lab Works

Species Registry: Each computational species has a genome (parameter dict) and a kernel (callable that produces a phenotype numpy array). The SPECIES_REGISTRY maps species names to (genome_factory, kernel) pairs:

  • julia_set - escape-time fractal on the complex plane (c parameter)
  • mandelbrot - canonical escape-time fractal, z=z^2+c iteration
  • gray_scott - reaction-diffusion Turing pattern simulator
  • rule30 - 1-D elementary cellular automaton
  • l_system - recursive string-rewriting turtle graphics renderer
  • dijkstra_field - multi-source Dijkstra shortest-path distance field

Hybridization Methods: The hybridize() function crosses two parent species:

  • fractal_seed - fractal boundary feeds into Gray-Scott initial conditions (U/V concentrations seeded by fractal distance)
  • ca_lsystem - L-system geometry seeds Rule 30 initial row (branch tips become active cells)
  • ca_fractal - fractal column perturbs Rule 30 initial state
  • lsystem_ca - CA density modulates L-system iteration depth
  • field_blend - alpha compositing of two spatial fields (alpha-weighted blend)

Extensibility: New species can be added by registering a genome factory and kernel in SPECIES_REGISTRY. New hybridization methods can be added to the hybridize() function. All hybrids are reproducible via parameterized genomes (seeds documented in metadata).
